description_block: This home NBA Pioneers Classic ‘Association Edition’ jersey was worn by Derrick White on February 1, 2026, when the Boston Celtics played the Milwaukee Bucks.  White finished with 17 points, 7 rebounds, 8 assists, and 1 steal. The Celtics beat the Bucks, 107-79.  The inaugural Pioneers Classic game honors those who broke the color barrier in 1950: Chuck Cooper, Nat Clifton and Earl Lloyd. Each player wore a jersey featuring a commemorative jersey patch as well as a “1950” patch on the back to honor this historic moment. Derrick White has been a game-changer for the Celtics on both ends of the court. In each of the past two seasons, he had career-best percentages from 3-point range and was named to the All-Defensive 2nd Team. His lockdown defense has helped the Celtics’ stifle opposing teams and roll to an NBA title in 2024.  Derrick White was drafted with the 29th pick in the first round of the 2017 NBA Draft out of The University of Colorado-Boulder. At the time of cataloging, he has career averages of 13.4 points per game, 3.8 rebounds per game, and 4.3 assists per game. White helped the Celtics win the 2024 NBA Championship. This jersey has been photomatched by Sotheby’s Photomatching.

auction_title: NBA Auctions Weekly: Road to the Championship
title: Chet Holmgren Oklahoma City Thunder Signed NBA Draft Hat
description_block: This Oklahoma City Thunder Draft Hat was signed by Chet Holmgren.  Drafted 2nd overall in the 1st round of the 2022 NBA Draft, Chet Holmgren has quickly emerged as a budding star in the NBA. Despite missing his first year due to injury, he has already showcased a rare blend of elite rim protection and perimeter shot-making. Holmgren became one of the league’s premier interior defenders, averaging 2.3 blocks per game during the 2023–24 season—his official rookie year. He finished second to Victor Wembanyama in the Rookie of the Year race and was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team. In just his second active season, Holmgren played a key role in helping lead the Oklahoma City Thunder to the 2025 NBA Championship —the franchise’s first title since relocating to Oklahoma City. Anchoring the defense and stretching the floor on offense, Holmgren proved to be a critical piece in the Thunder’s title run. With the emergence of the Thunder’s young “Big 3” of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams, and Chet Holmgren, Oklahoma City is no longer just a team of the future—it’s a powerhouse of the present, poised to build the NBA’s next great dynasty. At the time of cataloging, Holmgren has career averages of 16.5 points per game, 8.3 rebounds per game, and 2.1 assists per game. This lot is accompanied by a letter from JSA in regards to the signature.
